newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Wednesday as most investors continued to cling to the sidelines, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,299 yuan ($398) per tonne, rising 21 yuan. It opened at 3,300 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,320 and a low of 3,295.
July did not trade, September fell five yuan to 3,253, the January 1998 contract rose 60 to 3,300 and March dropped five to 3,2915 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 14,800 tonnes from 18,300 tonne.
Soybeans opened higher and moved at opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Later-maturing contracts consolidated around the 3,300 yuan level, indicating that many investors think the current prices are rational," one trader said.
"Trading was slow today because many investors paid more attention to active domestic stock markets," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the next few days.
